Hi Nikhil / Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — Orion is excited about Redwood's serving performance. Before procurement moves forward our security & ops teams need clear language about multi-region failover behavior and the operational obligations tied to the RTO/RPO numbers in the SOW. Two items to clarify: 

- During a region outage, what exact steps does Redwood take to route traffic to a standby region, and what manual steps (if any) are required from Orion?
- Can you confirm achievable RTO and RPO targets for our setup (real-time payments, key-value cacheing), and any limitations during peak traffic?

Our procurement window is tight — we need draft amendment language we can share with our legal team by EOD next week. I can share our production topology if that helps (I attached a simple diagram).

Hi Emily — thanks for the note and the topology. Attaching a draft amendment that lays out two options (hosted vs. dedicated) and the corresponding commitments. High level:

- Hosted (standard): automatic cross-region routing + warm-standby; target RTO 15 minutes, target RPO 1 hour; automatic prefix and KV cache rebuilding may add ~10–20s for initial tokens.
- Dedicated (premium): reserved multi-region capacity and active-active routing; target RTO 5 minutes during business hours, RPO 15 minutes; includes runbook, periodic DR tests, and a named on-call rotation.

I attached the proposed-sla-amendment.docx for legal redlines. Can you confirm whether Orion requires the 5-minute target or if an SLA credit would be acceptable? I'll coordinate with Karthik on the technical caveats.

—Nikhil

Subject: Re: Request: Clarify failover obligations and RTO/RPO for multi-region DR

Emily — quick technical note to make the constraints explicit so procurement has accurate expectations. High-level behavior: 

1) Detection and failover: Redwood monitors regional health via both infra heartbeats and model-serving health probes. On confirmed regional outage we trigger routing to the standby region. The DNS + edge propagation and our smart routing layer typically begin shifting traffic within seconds; total observed RTO depends on session rehydration and KV cache warmup.

2) RTO assumptions: The 15-minute RTO for Hosted assumes no active-long-lived sessions that require manual cache rehydration. For customers with hot KV caches (like real-time payments lookup tables), the actual end-to-end recovery to steady-state may be longer; we estimate 5–30 minutes depending on dataset size. Dedicated customers can have pre-warmed KV replicas to meet a 5-minute RTO during declared standby windows.

3) RPO assumptions: Cross-region asynchronous replication gives RPO on the order of 15–60 minutes depending on throughput and replication window. If Orion requires sub-15-minute RPO we recommend a synchronous replication path or periodic micro-checkpointing (add-on).

4) Operational responsibilities: Redwood will own routing and runbook execution for failover. Orion will need to validate that client-side timeouts/backpressure are tolerant of short-lived retries during switchover. We should include a short list of recommended client timeout settings in the amendment.

Happy to hop on a quick 30-min call with your ops team to align.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: Clarify failover obligations and RTO/RPO for multi-region DR

Thanks — the technical detail is helpful. Short follow-up from our legal/procurement side: Orion's risk committee is pushing for a firm 5-minute RTO during business hours (US PST 6am–6pm) for critical payment flows, or an alternate financial remedy (credits/penalty) that meaningfully offsets disruption risk. They also want to cap data divergence (RPO) at 15 minutes for those critical flows.

We are evaluating three things internally: (1) accept Redwood's Dedicated premium offering that matches 5min/15min with a higher spend, (2) ask Redwood to add a firm credit schedule into the SOW for Hosted, or (3) support a hybrid: Dedicated for critical endpoints + Hosted for bulk workloads.

Can Redwood provide draft credit language or confirm whether the Dedicated offering includes scheduled DR tests and a named on-call SLA? We need this for our internal approval by 11/12.

Appreciate it — Emily

Team — quick internal note before Nikhil sends a formal proposal to Orion. Position guidance: 

- We can offer two commercial pathways: (A) Hosted with SLA credit schedule tied to failover duration (example: 5% credit for outages >30m, 15% for >2h) with a documented runbook and annual DR test; (B) Dedicated Premium with documented 5min RTO during business hours, 15min RPO, quarterly DR tests and a named escalation contact.
- Legal should redline the proposed-sla-amendment.docx to ensure credit calculations are capped and force majeure carveouts are explicit.
- Commercial ask: push Orion toward Dedicated for critical payment endpoints; offer a 6-month pilot for hybrid setup to prove behavior.

Nikhil — please mirror this in the customer-facing amendment, include explicit client timeout recommendations, and request DocuSign acceptance for the Dedicated addendum. I'll loop Legal if Orion pushes for uncapped credits.

Thanks,
Neha

Hi Emily — appreciate the clarity on Orion's risk posture. Based on Neha and Karthik's input we've prepared two concrete options in the attached amendment (proposed-sla-amendment.docx) and summarized below so you can share with legal:

Option A — Hosted + SLA credits (lower cost):
- Target RTO: 15 minutes (automatic routing + warm-standby).
- Target RPO: 60 minutes.
- Financial remedy: tiered credit schedule tied to total failover time for critical endpoints; capped at 20% of monthly fees for any single incident.
- Deliverables: documented failover runbook, annual DR test, and recommended client timeout settings.

Option B — Dedicated Premium (recommended for critical payments):
- Target RTO: 5 minutes during business hours (6am–6pm PST) for defined critical endpoints.
- Target RPO: 15 minutes.
- Deliverables: pre-warmed KV replicas, quarterly DR tests, named escalation contact, and a 3-month hybrid pilot for migration validation.

Next steps: please indicate whether Orion prefers A (Hosted + credits) or B (Dedicated Premium). If B, we'll prepare a Dedicated addendum and send via DocuSign (link included below). If A, we will insert the credit schedule into the SOW and return for redline.
